text:
Oliver Bjorkstrand has 10 points in 18 games while playing about 11:30 a night, which is the most efficient scoring stretch of anyone on the Rangers' depth lines. He has six goals, two on the power play, and has been playing with J.T. Miller on the second line lately.

It won't keep going at this pace. His shooting percentage is 22.2%, his points per 60 (2.89) are well above the top of our range for him, and he has six goals on 4.1 expected. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season in Tampa Bay, and their model said offense wasn't really his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he rarely carries the puck in, so his lines lean on dump-ins and the forecheck.

There is something real underneath: the Rangers take about 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his "plays like" comparisons note that he keeps chances against down. Our range has him at 14 to 24 goals over a full season. Enjoy the run, and expect a quieter December.
headline: Bjorkstrand's hot start will cool
